name: people_en
items: A 16-year-old secondary-school student in Swansea, Wales, who helps care for her younger brother and mainly uses AI on a cracked Android phone.
A 17-year-old farm apprentice near Gorey, Ireland, who raises dairy calves and wants help writing clearer emails to suppliers.
An 18-year-old first-year engineering student in Manchester, England, who is the first in his family to attend university and enjoys repairing bicycles.
A 19-year-old supermarket night-shift worker in Perth, Australia, who is saving for nursing school and follows Korean cooking channels.
A 20-year-old unemployed school-leaver in Derry, Northern Ireland, who has dyslexia and is learning basic web design at a community centre.
A 21-year-old hospitality student in Wellington, New Zealand, who speaks Samoan at home and organises low-cost meals for flatmates.
A 22-year-old delivery cyclist in Toronto, Canada, who recently immigrated from Colombia and needs help understanding tenancy documents.
A 23-year-old trainee electrician in Birmingham, England, who plays five-a-side football and prefers short, practical instructions.

A 26-year-old junior accountant in Lagos, Nigeria, who commutes by bus, speaks Yoruba with family and is studying for professional exams.

A 34-year-old construction labourer in Christchurch, New Zealand, who left school at 16 and is preparing for a site-supervisor qualification.
A 35-year-old freelance translator in Athens, Greece, who works between Greek and English and collects vintage railway timetables.
A 36-year-old sheep farmer in Cumbria, England, who manages the farm with his sister and is cautious about online banking.
A 37-year-old public librarian in Tulsa, United States, who runs a weekly job-search clinic and makes pottery at weekends.
A 38-year-old dental receptionist in Belfast, Northern Ireland, who has three school-age children and coordinates the family's appointments from her phone.

A 40-year-old warehouse forklift operator in Rotterdam, Netherlands, who learned English at work and coaches a girls' handball team.

A 42-year-old community nurse in County Mayo, Ireland, who visits isolated patients and grows vegetables in a polytunnel.
A 43-year-old taxi driver in Queens, New York, who was born in Bangladesh and often dictates requests between airport pickups.
A 44-year-old civil servant in Canberra, Australia, who drafts procurement documents and sings in a neighbourhood choir.
A 45-year-old fisheries officer in Suva, Fiji, who travels among outer islands and needs documents that work offline.
A 46-year-old self-employed plumber in Leeds, England, who is excellent with customers but uncertain about spreadsheets and tax terminology.
A 47-year-old hotel housekeeper in Las Vegas, United States, who speaks Spanish at home and is helping her daughter apply to college.
A 48-year-old newspaper editor in Nairobi, Kenya, who follows county politics closely and keeps bees on a small plot outside the city.
A 49-year-old GP receptionist in a village near Norwich, England, who knows many patients personally and is meticulous about confidentiality.
A 50-year-old bus mechanic in Limerick, Ireland, who rebuilds classic radios and types slowly with two fingers.
A 51-year-old owner of a corner shop in Leicester, England, who orders stock before dawn and supports relatives in two countries.
A 52-year-old Aboriginal health worker in Alice Springs, Australia, who travels to remote communities and values plain, respectful language.
A 53-year-old university laboratory technician in Boston, United States, who maintains ageing equipment and cares for a partner with multiple sclerosis.

A 56-year-old housing-association officer in Cardiff, Wales, who mediates neighbour disputes and attends evening Welsh classes.
A 57-year-old machinist in Detroit, United States, who is retraining after his factory introduced computer-controlled equipment.
A 58-year-old market-stall owner in Singapore who sells fabric, speaks three languages and prefers examples over abstract explanations.
A 59-year-old special-needs classroom aide in Dunedin, New Zealand, who makes tactile learning materials and rarely uses social media.
A 60-year-old postal worker in rural Nova Scotia, Canada, who knows every back road and plans multi-day canoe trips.
A 61-year-old recently redundant travel agent in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, who is applying for office jobs after 30 years in one company.
A 62-year-old magistrates' court usher in London, England, who commutes from Essex and researches family history in parish archives.
A 63-year-old olive grower in Kalamata, Greece, who sells to English-speaking customers and relies on a nephew for computer troubleshooting.

A 70-year-old retired carpenter in County Clare, Ireland, who plays traditional fiddle and wants simple guidance for video calls.
A 71-year-old grandmother in rural Jamaica who manages a small poultry yard and asks relatives to print important online forms.
A 72-year-old retired chemistry lecturer in Oxford, England, who enjoys precise explanations and is learning to identify local moths.
A 73-year-old former seamstress in Melbourne, Australia, who volunteers at a repair café and uses large text on her laptop.
A 74-year-old retired postal clerk in Ohio, United States, who organises veterans' association lunches and worries about online scams.
A 75-year-old crofter on the Isle of Lewis, Scotland, who keeps a small flock, speaks Gaelic and checks email once each evening.
A 76-year-old retired hotel cook in Dublin, Ireland, who adapts old recipes for a low-salt diet and sends long voice-dictated messages.

An 81-year-old former nurse in Maine, United States, who coordinates rides for neighbours and prints every set of instructions.
An 82-year-old retired shopkeeper in Leicester, England, who speaks Gujarati at home and is compiling family recipes for great-grandchildren.
An 83-year-old former lighthouse keeper in County Donegal, Ireland, who records coastal weather in notebooks and uses a refurbished desktop computer.
An 84-year-old retired music teacher in Christchurch, New Zealand, who still accompanies a community choir and needs high-contrast documents.
An 85-year-old former council gardener in Plymouth, England, who shares a home with his son and enjoys identifying plants from old photographs.
